quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a crossbuck sign. What should you do?

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for a train.
Wait for a flagger to clear you, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must approach all railroad crossings carefully and cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, you must follow their instructions.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving toward.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they can see traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where it is allowed.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down faster.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to yield to trains. Do not try to drive around or beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right only after a complete stop.
No right turns are allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows a law you must follow. Right turns are not permitted at this location.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these choices

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving, including illegal drugs and prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This yield sign means you must slow down as you approach and give the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: When can you carefully go through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the yellow light appears, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
There is a stop sign.
Red flashing lights and gates are working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger tells you to, if there is a stop sign, or if red flashing lights and gates are working.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Broken white lines mean you can cross to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Can be stationary or moving.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving (like vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow). They are marked with orange signs with black letters. Always slow down and pay extra attention in work zones.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Red light that is flashing.
Yellow light that is steady.
Yellow arrow.
Yellow light that is flashing.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:

options.text: Optional.
Smart.
Safe.
Dangerous.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than the speed limit can be dangerous. It forces other drivers to take risks while trying to pass you.

questions.question: Where may a motorcycle operator use a complete traffic lane?

options.text: Only on rural highways
Only on city streets
On all highways and streets where motorcycles are allowed
Nowhere. Motorcyclists must share lanes with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all highways and streets where motorcycles are allowed
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have the right to use a complete lane on any road where motorcycles are allowed. However, two motorcyclists may choose to ride side by side in one lane.

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves sharply in the direction the arrow points (to the left). You may see several of these signs placed throughout the curve.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery roads. Safety may require driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
Can force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear to do so.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help make night driving safer?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you look into oncoming headlights, your pupils shrink. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway where stereo volume is limited.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the back, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Some crossings do not have these devices. It is against the law to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
Must go straight and cannot turn.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic first.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign forbidding it.

questions.question: You can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the road.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when there is a passing lane and the vehicle ahead is turning left or about to turn left. You can also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes going the same way. You can never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down and be prepared to stop. Look both ways and check all tracks before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop safely away from the tracks and wait until it passes.

questions.question: In fog, you should use high beam headlights to see better.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights. Do not use high beams as they reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When can you proceed through a stop sign intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic
After coming to a complete stop and confirming it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing down to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and confirming it is safe
questions.explanation: At any stop sign, stop before the stop line or crosswalk. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
School crossing ahead.
Do not use this lane.
Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign works with the traffic light to warn drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to pass first.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On long trips, stop every two hours for a short break. If you get drowsy, pull over and park safely to rest, nap, or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and/or flashing lights approaches you, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or warning devices approaches, drive to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams comes toward you, look toward the ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
Center
Right side
Left side

questions.explanation: If a vehicle is using high beams and does not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your lane until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light means red is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe passing on a two-way, two-lane street requires that you can see the road ahead clearly, return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and have a vehicle fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, not what the flagger says.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if construction was not happening.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Ignoring these directions is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: A good rule to remember for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another vehicle, the chance of a crash goes up. If you drive faster than others, you will have to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, stay within the legal speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.explanation: At intersections with signs, signals, or no controls, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right when both arrive at the same time.

questions.question: Your stereo volume should be low enough so you can hear traffic sounds.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Set your stereo volume before you drive. If you cannot hear normal traffic sounds, turn the volume down.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves to the right ahead.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Keep your tires filled to the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep tire tread depth good and tires at the correct pressure. Also slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds.

questions.question: What affects the space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights approaches on a one-way street, pull to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: To turn left on a multilane street or highway, start from the left lane.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area.
The highest or lowest legal speed allowed.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in poor conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed allowed.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. These limits are for ideal conditions. You must drive slower when conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels left.
Turn your wheels right.
Stop parallel to the car in front of the space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the car in front of the space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and signaling, stop parallel to the car directly in front of your desired space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that extend up to 200 feet directly behind them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate large vehicles because drivers cannot see you.
